subject: Huxton: investigating persistent tail latency and proposed interim mitigations
messages:
From: Max Chen <max@huxton.com>

Cc: ops@huxton.com
Date: Tue, 28 Sep 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Spike in checkout generation P99/P995 — seeing drop in conversions

Hi Aisha,

We started seeing recurring spikes yesterday evening (P99 and occasional P995) on the checkout personalization endpoint that powers our upsell modal. Spike shows up as long-tail latency (~4-8s tails) and correlates with a ~6% drop in conversion rate during the windows.

This is hitting our busiest region (US-west) and appears to come in bursts — not sustained high load overall. Attached is a short CSV with p95/p99 samples from our side. Can you confirm whether this aligns with anything on Redwood's side (queueing/backpressure or concurrency caps)? We need a quick mitigation while you investigate deeper.

Thanks,
Max
Customer Success — Huxton Retail

Hi Max — thanks for the heads up and the data. Sorry you're seeing this.

I’m looping in Laura (SRE lead) and Dylan (runtime on-call) to correlate telemetry. Can you confirm:
- whether the spikes map to a particular model version or route?
- approximate percentage of traffic routed to the checkout route during the windows?

As an interim mitigation we can:
- temporarily increase concurrency cap for that route for the next 4–12 hours;
- enable prefix caching for repeated invoice prompts (if applicable);
- failover that route to a compatible lower-memory variant if caps appear saturated.

We’ll aim for an initial response and recommended action within 2 hours.

— Aisha

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>

Date: Tue, 28 Sep 2027 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Spike in checkout generation P99/P995 — seeing drop in conversions

Hi all,

We pulled early telemetry: the service-level metrics show periodic queue depth spikes on the dedicated pool serving Huxton (pool-id: ded-usw-8). The spike windows line up with the CSV Max sent. Initial hypothesis: occasional request bursts are hitting a concurrency cap on the route and causing request queuing/backpressure inside the runtime; when queue length grows, tail latency balloons.

What we see:
- background throughput steady; bursts are short (~30s–2m)
- CPU/GPU utilization on the pool stays moderate (40–60%), latency jump seems driven by queueing and KV-cache warmup churn
- small fraction (0.7%) of requests are getting a 429 from the route limiter during the peak windows (this correlates with the client-side retries)

Immediate ask for on-call (Dylan): can you grab the runtime logs for the route between 2027-09-27T22:40Z and 2027-09-27T23:00Z UTC and check span breakdowns for queue_wait vs service_time?

Also copying Marcus for potential short-term capacity bump approval.

— Laura
SRE Lead, Redwood Inference
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.com>
Cc: Max Chen <max@huxton.com>
Date: Tue, 28 Sep 2027 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Spike in checkout generation P99/P995 — seeing drop in conversions

Laura — pulling traces now. Early snippet:

--- LOG EXCERPT (forwarded) ---
From: runtime-ded-usw-8
Time: 2027-09-27T22:46:17Z
Route: /v1/generate/checkout-upsel
queue_wait_ms: 2100
service_ms: 320
kv_cache_miss: true
concurrency_slot_wait_ms: 1800
429_emitted: false
--- end excerpt ---

This looks like requests are waiting for concurrency slots (concurrency_slot_wait_ms non-trivial) while service_time remains reasonable. We also have a pattern where KV-cache churn (misses) on some long tails amplifies the queueing.

My proposed immediate actions:
1) Increase route concurrency cap from 100 -> 150 for the Huxton route in ded-usw-8 for the next 6 hours.
2) Temporarily enable an aggressive KV-prefetch policy for that route to reduce cold misses.
3) Enable a soft-fail fallback to a lower-precision quantized variant for requests exceeding a 3s queue wait.

I’ll start action 1 now if Marcus signs off.

— Dylan
Runtime On-call

Subject: Re: Spike in checkout generation P99/P995 — seeing drop in conversions

Hi Max — quick update and next steps:

What we did (completed 2027-09-28 13:10 PDT):
- Increased concurrency cap for /v1/generate/checkout-upsel from 100 -> 150 (window: 6 hours).
- Enabled KV-prefetch policy for the route and warmed cache for the hot prefixes.
- Deployed soft-fail policy to route requests with queue_wait > 3000ms to the quantized variant.

Early outcome: P99 dropped from ~4200ms -> ~950ms in the follow-up 2-hour window; P995 occurrences reduced by ~85%. Customer-side conversion metrics returned to baseline within the mitigation window.

Next steps (72-hour plan):
- Laura/Dylan: deep root-cause analysis to determine if queueing is caused by an under-provisioned slot allocation algorithm vs unusually bursty client behavior. Deliverable: RCA + config recommendations by 2027-10-01 11:00 PDT.
- Product Ops (Marcus/Sean): propose permanent routing policy change or capacity plan if we see recurring bursts.
- Offer: Redwood will provide a one-time service credit for the affected windows; Sean will draft the exec note and I will send it to your CTO.

Attachments: runbook_interim_mitigation.md (md)

Thanks for being patient — will keep you posted.

— Aisha
Account Lead, Redwood Inference
